mission: Establish the first local pedagogical foundations corpus for the Teacher Mind so tutoring rests on serious explanation design, guidance, feedback, and instructional sequencing before mathematics-specific specialization.
collection_principles: Prefer institutional practice guides and major synthesis papers before many narrow instructional studies.
Translate pedagogical evidence into concrete tutoring moves such as modeling, guided practice, fading, feedback, and progression design.
Treat pedagogy as a discipline of explanation quality and learner support, not just content delivery.
Include guardrails against popular but weak or mistimed instructional patterns.
core_questions: How should a tutor sequence an explanation so understanding can form step by step?
When should a tutor model, guide, prompt, and then fade support?
What role do worked examples and self-explanations play in building competence?
What makes feedback learning-improving rather than merely evaluative?
How much guidance should novices receive before independent problem solving is expected?

domains.name: Explanation Design
domains.goal: Ground the structure and sequencing of explanations.

domains.name: Guidance and Scaffolding
domains.goal: Guide how strongly the tutor should lead and when support should be reduced.

domains.name: Worked Examples and Fading
domains.goal: Support model-first instruction for novices and progressive fading toward independent control.

domains.name: Feedback and Formative Assessment
domains.goal: Improve the tutor's feedback style, understanding checks, and instructional adaptation.

domains.name: Instructional Progression
domains.goal: Guide movement from concrete support toward abstract and formal mastery.

domains.name: Anti-Pattern Guardrails
domains.goal: Prevent the Teacher Mind from defaulting to under-guided or poorly sequenced instruction.

starter_sources.title: Organizing Instruction and Study to Improve Student Learning
starter_sources.organization: Institute of Education Sciences / What Works Clearinghouse
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Core guide for spacing, interleaving worked examples with problem solving, combining graphics with words, and connecting abstract and concrete representations.

starter_sources.title: Using Student Achievement Data to Support Instructional Decision Making
starter_sources.organization: Institute of Education Sciences / What Works Clearinghouse
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Important baseline for ongoing cycles of instructional improvement, student goal-setting, and adapting teaching to evidence of learning.

starter_sources.title: Principles of Instruction: Research-Based Strategies That All Teachers Should Know
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Widely used synthesis of explicit instruction, small steps, guided practice, questioning, checks for understanding, and gradual release of difficulty.

starter_sources.title: The Power of Feedback
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Major review clarifying that feedback can help or harm, and that task, process, and self-regulation feedback differ sharply from praise-level responses.

starter_sources.title: Focus on Formative Feedback
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Important synthesis for feedback that is specific, supportive, timely, and oriented toward changing learner thinking or behavior.

starter_sources.title: Self-Explanations: How Students Study and Use Examples in Learning to Solve Problems
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Foundational source for how learners use worked examples and why self-explanation strengthens transfer beyond copying steps.

starter_sources.title: Why Minimal Guidance During Instruction Does Not Work
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Major guardrail source against expecting novices to learn efficiently from under-guided instruction before they have sufficient internal structure.
